material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Foundation Primer

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry & Stucco Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY on ALL new concrete/CMU foundation — pH 12-14 requires alkali-resistant primer. Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable. SW Loxon is rated to pH 13, enabling 7-day accelerated coating (vs 28-day standard cure). Poured concrete coverage is higher (300-350 SF/gal) due to denser, smoother surface than typical masonry wall. CMU coverage after block filler is comparable (275-350 SF/gal). Same product class as masonry wall primer.

material_systems.notes: Non-negotiable primer for new foundation. Alkali-resistance is not quality-optional — even QT2 must use this primer. Coverage is better than masonry wall primer on poured concrete because foundation concrete is denser with less porosity than brick or rough CMU.

material_systems.name: Block Filler for CMU Foundation (PCA P12 Level 2 Standard Fill)

specialty.notes: Mandatory for CMU foundation — fills open-cell voids to PCA P12 Level 2 (max 10 voids per SF). Not a primer — substrate preparation product applied BEFORE alkali-resistant primer. Heavy-body material requiring 527-535 spray tip (0.025-0.035 orifice) and 30-mesh coarse filter. Pressure: 2,300-3,000 PSI. Backroll mandatory after spray to force filler into voids. Same requirement as masonry wall spec.

material_systems.notes: CMU foundation without block filler will have voids that telegraph through primer and finish coats. Coverage is very low (75-125 SF/gal) due to void filling — the most material-intensive step. QT level does not affect block filler application — always required on CMU regardless of tier.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Foundation Coating

finish.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior for above-grade cosmetic foundation coating. UV-resistant. 10-20 perms breathability preserves vapor diffusion. Foundation concrete is relatively smooth (smoother than masonry wall), yielding higher coverage (300-400 SF/gal) than masonry wall acrylic (200-350 SF/gal). QT2 allows single finish coat on properly primed surface. QT3 requires two coats. Wider color range and satin option available vs cementitious.

material_systems.notes: Primary finish system for residential foundation. Flat is budget standard for utilitarian foundation band. Satin for higher-end residential where foundation appearance matters on showcase elevations. Coverage is higher than masonry wall due to smoother poured concrete substrate.

material_systems.name: Cementitious Waterproof Coating (Drylok-type)

finish.notes: Cementitious/crystalline coating for moisture-prone foundation areas. Withstands up to 15 PSI hydrostatic pressure. Crystalline technology seals capillaries in concrete. Thicker application (10-15 mils DFT) than acrylic, yielding lower coverage (150-200 SF/gal). Breathable, matte finish only. Excellent adhesion to concrete. Budget-friendly material cost but heavier application. Alternative to acrylic for areas with moisture exposure.

material_systems.notes: Cementitious coatings are inherently flat/matte due to film thickness and chemistry. Good for utilitarian foundation where moisture resistance is the priority over aesthetics. Drylok-type products are well-suited to above-grade cosmetic coating with moisture-proofing benefit. No satin/semi-gloss option — flat only.

poured_concrete.notes: Poured concrete foundation — dense, relatively smooth surface with low porosity. Higher primer coverage than masonry wall substrates. Bug holes and form marks may reduce coverage slightly.

CMU_filled.notes: CMU after block filler application — surface is sealed by filler, improving primer coverage. Comparable to poured concrete.

assumptions: Coverage rates are for roll application. Spray adds 25% material for transfer efficiency loss.
Poured concrete assumes form-release agents and laitance have been removed per prep sequence.
CMU coverage assumes block filler has been applied. Unfiltered CMU primer coverage would be much lower.

CMU.notes: CMU block filler coverage varies by void density and block profile. Standard-weight CMU: ~100 SF/gal. Lightweight/open-texture CMU: as low as 75 SF/gal.

assumptions: Coverage is for single coat block filler application with spray + backroll.
Spray application: transfer efficiency is low (~50-60%) due to heavy-body material — already factored into range.
CMU only — not applicable to poured concrete foundation.

poured_concrete_primed.notes: Finish coat on primed poured concrete — smooth substrate yields best coverage. Primer seals porosity.

CMU_filled_primed.notes: Finish coat on filled and primed CMU. Block filler + primer creates well-sealed surface.

assumptions: Coverage per coat. Two-coat system at QT3 doubles material consumption.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25 for transfer efficiency loss.
Assumes proper primer application has sealed substrate porosity.

poured_concrete_primed.notes: Cementitious coating on primed poured concrete — heavier application (10-15 mils DFT) yields lower coverage than acrylic.

CMU_filled_primed.notes: Cementitious coating on filled and primed CMU. CMU texture consumes slightly more material than smooth poured concrete.

assumptions: Coverage per coat. Two-coat system at QT3 doubles material consumption.
Cementitious coatings are typically applied by roll or brush — not spray. Roll is the primary method.
Heavier DFT (10-15 mils) is the primary driver of lower coverage vs acrylic (4-6 mils).

consumables.name: Roller cover 3/4 to 1 inch nap (foundation)
consumables.notes: Medium-heavy nap roller for foundation surfaces. 3/4 inch nap for smooth poured concrete, 1 inch nap for CMU. Nylon/polyester blend for water-based products. Smaller nap than masonry wall roller (1-1/4 inch) because foundation concrete is smoother.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 517 (foundation acrylic/primer)
consumables.notes: Standard 0.017 orifice for acrylic latex and alkali-resistant primer on foundation. Cementitious substrate causes faster tip wear than wood.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 531 (block filler)
consumables.notes: 0.025-0.035 orifice (527-535 range) for heavy-body block filler on CMU foundation. Requires 2,300-3,000 PSI. CMU only — not needed for poured concrete.

consumables.name: 60-mesh spray filter (black) for latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh filter for acrylic exterior coatings and alkali-resistant primer. Change when flow rate drops.

consumables.name: 30-mesh spray filter (gray/coarse) for block filler
consumables.notes: Coarse 30-mesh filter for block filler. Heavy-body material clogs standard 60-mesh filters. CMU only.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting for exterior protection (4 mil UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum thickness. UV-resistant. Used for landscape perimeter overspray protection and hardscape coverage. Foundation is a small scope — typically 1-2 rolls.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for adjacent hardscape walkway and patio protection. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Red stucco poly tape (7.0 mil, 30-day UV)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 ROLL (60 yd) per 50 LF of masking lines
consumables.notes: For masking on textured CMU foundation surfaces. Standard blue tape will NOT adhere to rough CMU. 7.0 mil thickness, 30-day UV rating. CMU only — poured concrete uses standard blue tape.

consumables.name: Painter's tape (exterior grade, UV-resistant)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 ROLL per 60 LF of masking lines
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum. Used for masking on smooth poured concrete foundation and for masking the grade-line gap. Blue tape is suitable on smooth surfaces only — for CMU, use CON_FNDN_STUCCO_TAPE. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) cleaner
consumables.notes: For foundation cleaning and form-release agent removal on poured concrete. TSP solution applied with stiff brush, rinsed thoroughly. Also for efflorescence treatment. At QT2, water wash may substitute for light cleaning.

consumables.name: Wire brush for form-release agent removal
consumables.notes: For mechanical removal of form-release agents and laitance on poured concrete foundation. Also used for efflorescence dry brushing. Poured concrete only — CMU uses stiff bristle brush.

consumables.name: Stiff bristle masonry brush
consumables.notes: Heavy-duty stiff bristle brush for CMU foundation prep, efflorescence removal, and general cleaning. Poly or tampico bristle — not wire (wire can embed in mortar joints and rust). Replace when bristles flatten.

consumables.name: Hydraulic cement for bug holes and form ties
consumables.notes: For patching bug holes, form tie holes, and honeycombing on poured concrete foundation. Quick-setting hydraulic cement. Poured concrete primarily — CMU uses block filler for void filling. Small quantity needed for typical foundation band.

ext_landscape_perimeter.description: Foundation perimeter where landscape is adjacent — measured in LF along foundation wall base
ext_landscape_perimeter.notes: LF-based. Lay tarps along the perimeter where landscape beds, shrubs, and plants are adjacent to foundation wall. Spray: full tarp width over plantings (10-15 ft overspray drift). Roll/brush: narrower coverage at base.

ext_hardscape_walk.description: Adjacent walkways requiring protection from overspray and drips
ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray on areas without foot traffic.

ext_hardscape_patio.notes: Protection level driven by proximity and application method. Spray requires wider coverage than roll-only.

compatibility_rules.description: Oil-based and alkyd products PROHIBITED on alkaline concrete/CMU foundation
compatibility_rules.notes: Alkaline hydroxides (pH 12-14) react with alkyd/oil paint esters through saponification — hydrolyzing binder into soft, sticky, water-soluble soap. Complete removal to bare substrate is the only remedy. Same blocker rule as masonry wall spec.

compatibility_rules.description: Moisture content must be at or below 4% before any coating
compatibility_rules.required_action: Moisture test with electronic meter at multiple points. MC > 4% = HARD STOP
compatibility_rules.notes: Stricter than masonry wall spec (12%) due to continuous ground contact and capillary moisture rise through foundation. Foundation walls are in direct ground contact — higher moisture risk than above-grade masonry walls. Test at multiple points across the above-grade band.

compatibility_rules.description: NEVER caulk the 3/8-inch grade-line gap below siding
compatibility_rules.notes: The grade-line gap with Z-flashing is an intentional drainage plane. Caulking seals the drainage path, trapping moisture behind siding — causes catastrophic rot, mold, and structural damage. This is the #1 grade-line failure mode. Mask the gap during painting, do not fill it.

compatibility_rules.description: Concrete Surface Profile (CSP) must match coating thickness
compatibility_rules.required_action: CSP 1-2 for thin cosmetic coatings (<10 mils). CSP 3-5 for heavy coatings (40+ mils — out of scope for this spec).
compatibility_rules.notes: Above-grade cosmetic coating in this spec requires CSP 1-2 (smooth to light profile). 83% of foundation coating failures originate from insufficient surface roughness per doctrine. For poured concrete, form-release removal achieves adequate CSP.

risk_notes.risk: Coating applied over active efflorescence traps salt migration path. Salts continue to move through the concrete and accumulate behind the coating film, creating osmotic pressure that lifts the coating in bubbles. Foundation walls are particularly susceptible due to continuous ground contact and capillary moisture rise.
risk_notes.mitigation: Remove all efflorescence before coating. Verify MC <= 4% at coating surface. Do not coat foundation with active moisture migration.

risk_notes.risk: Caulking the 3/8-inch gap between siding and foundation seals the drainage plane. Moisture trapped behind siding causes rot, mold, and structural damage. This is a CATASTROPHIC failure that damages the building structure, not just the coating.
risk_notes.mitigation: NEVER caulk the siding-to-foundation gap. Mask the gap during painting. Educate homeowner/GC that the gap is intentional drainage.

risk_notes.topic: Adhesion failure from form-release agents on poured concrete
risk_notes.risk: Poured concrete retains waxy/oily form-release agents from the casting process. These bond-breakers prevent coating adhesion. Coating applied over form-release agents will peel off in sheets within weeks.
risk_notes.mitigation: Clean poured concrete foundation with TSP or degreaser. Wire brush or abrade surface to remove laitance and form-release residue. Verify adhesion with tape test on small area before full application.

risk_notes.topic: UV degradation of below-grade products used above grade
risk_notes.risk: Below-grade waterproofing products (bituminous, asphalt-based) are not UV-stable. If below-grade coating extends above grade line, painting contractor must NOT topcoat with standard paint over incompatible below-grade product.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use only UV-resistant coatings for above-grade foundation. Identify existing coating type before application if any below-grade coating is visible above grade.

risk_notes.topic: Saponification from oil-based products on alkaline concrete
risk_notes.risk: Oil-based or alkyd paints on alkaline foundation (pH 12-14) undergo saponification — alkaline hydroxides hydrolyze paint esters into soft, sticky, water-soluble soap. Complete removal to bare concrete is the only remedy.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use ONLY water-based acrylic or cementitious products. Alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_FNDN_PRIMER_ALKALI) as first coat. Never substitute standard primer.

material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on foundation: 60-70% transfer efficiency. Foundation is smoother than masonry wall, yielding slightly better transfer. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.25 for overspray and pattern overlap. Block filler spray: closer to 50-60% transfer due to heavy-body material.
material_quantity_notes.coat_count_standard: Block filler: 1 coat (CMU only). Alkali-resistant primer: 1 coat (all substrates). Finish acrylic: QT2=1 coat, QT3=2 coats. Finish cementitious: QT2=1 coat, QT3=2 coats.
material_quantity_notes.typical_foundation_material_stack_poured: Poured concrete at QT3 acrylic: 1 coat primer (325 SF/gal) + 2 coats finish (375 SF/gal each). For 400 SF foundation band (200 LF perimeter x 24-inch band): ~1.2 gal primer + ~2.1 gal finish = ~3.3 gal total. Small material scope.
material_quantity_notes.typical_foundation_material_stack_cmu_qt: CMU at QT3 acrylic: 1 coat block filler (100 SF/gal) + 1 coat primer (300 SF/gal) + 2 coats finish (325 SF/gal each). For 400 SF CMU foundation: ~4 gal filler + ~1.3 gal primer + ~2.5 gal finish = ~7.8 gal total.
material_quantity_notes.small_scope_note: Foundation band is typically 12-36 inches tall with limited surface area. A 200 LF perimeter with 24-inch band = 400 SF total. Material quantities are small — typically under 5 gallons total for poured concrete, under 10 gallons for CMU including block filler.

assumptions.value: 300-350 SF/gal — higher than masonry wall primer coverage
assumptions.note: Poured concrete foundation is denser and smoother than brick or rough CMU, yielding less absorption and better coverage.
Same as masonry wall spec. Coverage varies by void density. Conservative midpoint (100 SF/gal) used for estimation.
Doctrine does not specify exact coverage for Drylok-type cementitious coatings on foundation. Derived from DFT requirement (10-15 mils) and manufacturer data. Flag for field calibration.

assumptions.value: 300-400 SF/gal — higher than masonry wall finish coverage
assumptions.note: Foundation concrete is relatively smooth with primer sealing porosity. Coverage is better than rough masonry wall substrates.

assumptions.value: Red stucco poly tape required for masking on textured CMU foundation
assumptions.source: Masonry wall spec pattern; field experience
assumptions.note: Same as masonry wall spec. Standard blue tape does not adhere to rough CMU texture. Poured concrete can use standard blue tape.

assumptions.value: Reduced consumable set vs masonry wall spec — no HVAC/light fixture protection, no intercoat sanding
assumptions.note: Foundation is a small add-on spec. Ground-level work with limited adjacent surface risk. Protection zones are minimal (landscape perimeter, hardscape only). No QT4 means no intercoat sanding consumables needed.

uncertainty_flags.description: Exact SF/gal for Drylok-type cementitious coatings on foundation is not established in doctrine. Manufacturer PDS data varies (100-250 SF/gal). DFT-based calculation (10-15 mils) suggests 150-200 SF/gal. Field calibration needed.
uncertainty_flags.impact: Material quantity estimates for cementitious coating may be off by 15-25%. Budget conservatively.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Field calibration data from 3-5 cementitious foundation coating projects.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Block filler coverage variability on foundation CMU
uncertainty_flags.description: Foundation CMU may differ from wall CMU in block weight and void pattern. Industry range approximately 75-125 SF/gal. Using 100 SF/gal midpoint same as masonry wall spec.
uncertainty_flags.impact: Low — foundation CMU is typically standard-weight block with predictable void density.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Field measurement on foundation-specific CMU if coverage deviates from masonry wall experience.
